title: Where does ten thousand go in the chart?
description: Harpreet looks at the place value chart on her classroom wall in Amritsar. The video adds a new column and writes ten thousand with its comma.
teaching_notes: One idea: ten thousands make one in a new column, with four zeros to its right. Watch for the comma counted from the left.

source: Write ten thousand in the place value chart and say how many
video_script.why: The child knows the ones, tens, hundreds and thousands columns but has not met the column that comes next.
video_script.substitution: Use the rule that ten of one place make one of the next place to the left, then name the new column and place the comma.
video_script.anchor: the place value chart on Harpreet's classroom wall in Amritsar
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu counts three digits from the left and puts the comma there. The comma sits after the thousands place, three places from the right.
video_script.payoff_line: ten thousand is a one in the new column with four zeros after it

final_answer.value: 1 TTh and four zeros, written 10,000, which is 10 thousands
final_answer.spoken: one in the new column and four zeros, written with the comma, ten thousand

never_show: the your-turn answer 1 in the Th column and three zeros
maths_rules: 10 ones = 1 ten = 10; 10 tens = 1 hundred = 100; 10 hundreds = 1 thousand = 1,000
the new column is TTh (ten thousands), to the left of Th
the chart for ten thousand: TTh 1, Th 0, H 0, T 0, O 0
the comma sits after the Th place, three places from the right: 10,000
slip: counting three digits from the left gives 100,00, which is wrong
your turn: ten hundreds make a thousand, written in the chart as Th 1, H 0, T 0, O 0 = 1,000; never shown
video_script.design: One idea: ten of one place make one of the next place, so ten thousand needs a new column on the left. Wrong idea: the comma counted from the left. The wall chart stays as the anchor; the new column builds on the stage.
